newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares soft but stable at opening.
newsitem.headline: German shares soft but stable at opening.

text.p: German shares started bourse trade just lower on Tuesday, as the faltering dollar weighed on sentiment, but dealers predicted a calm day ahead as a "wait and see" attitude prevailed among investors.
The 30-share blue chip DAX index started down 5.16 points at 2,646.69 and was well supported around the 2,640 level, dealers said, noting there was no concerted selling pressure.

"We are low on economic news, low on corporate news. This market is really still drawing breath after the push upward we had last week," said a Munich dealer, who predicted the DAX would range from 2,640 to 2,655 during the day.
The prospect of Germany's public holiday on Thursday, which marks the country's unification, was also helping to keep activity low.
Stocks in the limelight included carmaker BMW which is to hold a news conference at the Paris Motor Show at 1100 GMT on Tuesday. The news conference was hastily announced on Tuesday.

Dealers speculated BMW will make an announcement about its Rover unit, possibly on vehicle marketing, personnel or on plans for a new British engine factory. BMW shares were 50 pfennigs ahead at 874 marks in early dealings.
Some attention was also focused on U.S. data due, including U.S. leading indicator data due at 1230 GMT.
